phases.name: Gravity-dominated motion in a rarefied atmosphere
phases.description: The vehicle enters the Martian atmosphere, where the upper atmosphere is still too rarefied to generate significant aerodynamic forces and heating.

phases.name: Aerothermal build-up
phases.description: As atmospheric density increases, aerodynamic drag and heating rise rapidly, marking the onset of significant aerothermal effects.

phases.name: Peak heating and aerodynamic load
phases.description: The vehicle encounters its most severe thermal environment and largest aerodynamic loads as velocity remains high in denser layers of the atmosphere.

phases.name: Hypersonic glide control phase
phases.description: The vehicle uses bank-angle control during hypersonic flight to shape its trajectory, manage energy, and maximize parachute deployment altitude.

phases.name: SUFR: “Straighten Up and Fly Right”
phases.description: The vehicle ejects balance masses to achieve near-zero angle of attack and reorients for safe parachute deployment and onboard radar altimeter ground acquisition.
